area: ADR-054 Phase D frontend (MiniApp tab/host call, preview-column collapse, MiniApps section, canvas menu, tutorial route) in /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d
how_you_tried:
Ran the two required commands from /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/frontend: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with no output; `npx vitest run` exits 0 with 233 files / 2600 tests passed (the only stderr is pre-existing jsdom canvas noise from @xterm). Note `--reporter=basic` no longer exists in vitest 4 and fails at startup, so the default reporter was used.

Then I read the real code rather than trusting the suite, and chased each of the named hunt items to its production call site rather than its unit test.

Tab-kind chains: closeTab/captureActiveTab/restoreTab/dropInactivePreviewTabs/syncActiveTab/TabBar/partialize all handle `miniapp` explicitly and correctly — teardown is genuinely unmount-driven via PanelFrame's effect cleanup, and `contexts.py:close()` does call `_stop`, so closing the tab, closing the project and switching projects all end panel.py. No accidental-pass there. I did find one non-exhaustive chain that a new kind falls through (the promotion confirm dialog's noun).

Preview column: `useMiniAppPreviewColumn` is correct on its own terms — it skips a column the user had already collapsed, records nothing to restore in that case, and refuses to re-collapse a column the user dragged open. I broke it from the other side instead: `openAllPreviewers` claims to expand a collapsed column via `previewCollapsed`, and grep shows nothing anywhere reads that flag to drive the panel.

Reload path: the reload does replace the frame (key on `<PanelFrame>` → new context → new iframe key), so the one-shot bootstrap handshake is safe. But the same `requestKey` mechanism that makes the reload work also fires on a `wsClientId` change, which is how I found the reconnect defect.

Call errors: `callResult` in lib/api/panels.ts does reject HTTP 200 `{error:...}`, and the SDK has a second (now unreachable) guard. Clean.

Context renewal: PanelFrame heartbeats `renew` every 240 s against the 600 s TTL for as long as it is mounted. Clean — the context dies on reconnect, not on TTL.

Prop shapes: I diffed the frontend MiniApp types against the Pydantic models in src/scistudio/api/routes/panels.py (MiniAppSummary/MiniAppSource/MiniAppCreated, `extra="forbid"` bodies) — they match, and `response.source` → `target` is mapped correctly. The mismatches I found are not type-level (tsc is green); they are call sites that accept a value and drop it (`session_tab_id`) and a component whose props are never passed at all (the canvas menu).

I could not exercise a live backend, so the two P1s are reasoned from code plus the backend's own comments, not observed in a running app.

defects.summary: Every WebSocket reconnect kills and respawns each open MiniApp's panel.py twice and wipes its page state; the frontend never sends the ?client_id= the backend added specifically to prevent this.
defects.repro:
frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:75 builds the socket URL as `wsUrl("/ws")` with no query string, and :141 (`handleClosed`) calls `handleWsDisconnected` → `setWsClientId(null)`. frontend/src/miniapps/MiniAppTab.tsx:95 puts `ws_client_id` inside the PanelFrame `request`; frontend/src/panels/PanelFrame.tsx:46 computes `requestKey = JSON.stringify(props.request)` and :130 makes it a dependency of the effect whose cleanup (:84-95) DELETEs the context — which src/scistudio/panels/contexts.py:460 `close()` turns into `_stop(context)`, ending panel.py.

User repro: open a MiniApp, then do anything that drops the socket — shut the laptop lid, restart the dev backend, or miss one 10 s heartbeat pong (useWebSocket.ts:115-119). `wsClientId` goes id → null → newId, so `requestKey` changes twice: the running context is deleted and recreated, then deleted and recreated again. The tab stays open (FR-019 at the tab level) but the frame reloads from scratch and the Python process is killed twice, losing whatever the process had loaded and whatever the page had on screen.

What makes this a defect rather than a trade-off: src/scistudio/api/ws.py:254-273 exists to avoid exactly this — "Such a client reconnects quoting the id it was given, and gets it back — so its MiniApp processes, which may hold a large array that took a minute to load, survive a flaky connection rather than being rebuilt from scratch." `_CLIENT_ID = re.compile(r"ws-[0-9a-f]{16}\Z")` accepts the minted shape on `?client_id=`. Grep across frontend/src shows the string `client_id` only in the hello reader — nothing ever sends it, and the store value is cleared before a reconnect could quote it. Additionally, any context created during the reconnect gap carries no `ws_client_id` at all, so FR-013's grace-period sweep has nothing to key that process on and it outlives the workspace.

defects.summary: FR-035's canvas block context menu is dead code: the only production render of WorkflowCanvas passes none of its three MiniApp props, and the component's own guard turns the feature off.
defects.repro:
frontend/src/components/WorkflowCanvas.tsx:255-262 declares `miniApps`, `onOpenMiniApp` and `onNewMiniApp` as optional props, and :690-692 guards the handler with `if (!onNewMiniApp && !onOpenMiniApp) return;` before `event.preventDefault()`. The sole production render site is `CanvasOrEditor` at frontend/src/App.parts/ProjectWorkspace.tsx:433-467, which passes 24 props and none of those three. Grep for `onNewMiniApp` / `onOpenMiniApp` / `miniApps=` across frontend/src returns only WorkflowCanvas.tsx itself, WorkflowCanvas.test.tsx, and the unrelated toolbar `onNewMiniApp` (a zero-arg `() => setCreateMiniAppOpen(true)` at App.tsx:416, which is FR-037, not FR-035).

User repro: open a project, run a block that produces an output, right-click the block node on the canvas. You get Chrome's own context menu. There is no "Open in <MiniApp>" and no "New MiniApp", and a block with no outputs never shows the disabled entries or the NO_OUTPUTS_REASON text FR-035 requires.

Two further FRs fall with it. FR-034's context-menu half ("Opening from a block's context menu MUST use that block's output, asking only when several ports match") is unreachable — the in-canvas MiniAppTargetPicker with `restrictTo` at WorkflowCanvas.tsx:723-740 can never open. And FR-023's pre-filled target is unreachable: `presetTarget` on CreateMiniAppDialog (frontend/src/miniapps/CreateMiniAppDialog.tsx:141) is passed by nothing outside CreateMiniAppDialog.test.tsx, because the store only carries the boolean `createMiniAppOpen` (frontend/src/store/uiSlice.ts:134) with no slot for a target, and ProjectWorkspace.tsx:795-798 mounts the dialog without it. WorkflowCanvas.test.tsx passes the props itself, which is why 2600 green tests say nothing about this.

defects.summary: FR-025 is not met: the agent session spawned by MiniApp create (and by Convert) is never registered or shown, so the user never sees the agent writing the MiniApp.
defects.repro:
frontend/src/App.parts/ProjectWorkspace.tsx:799-808 — `onCreated={(result) => { setCreateOpen(false); openMiniAppTab({panelId, name, target}); }}`. `result.session_tab_id` is carried all the way from the backend (src/scistudio/api/routes/panels.py:184-196 `MiniAppCreated.session_tab_id`) through miniapps/api.ts:29 and CreateMiniAppDialog.tsx:261, and is then dropped on the floor. The same happens for Convert at ProjectWorkspace.tsx:828 (`onStarted={() => setConvertFor(null)}`) even though ConvertToBlockDialog.tsx:157 passes `response.session_tab_id`.

FR-025 (docs/specs/adr-054-miniapp.md:493) requires the frontend to open the tab "and MUST show the agent session in the bottom AI tab". The established mechanism is two calls, used by the sibling surface at frontend/src/components/BringInMyWorkDialog.tsx:273-279: `addWorkImportTerminalTab({tabId, title, provider, permissionMode})` followed by `openBottomTab("ai")`. Grep shows `addWorkImportTerminalTab` has exactly one caller — BringInMyWorkDialog — so the MiniApp session is not merely unfocused, it is never joined in the UI at all.

User repro: MiniApps tab → New MiniApp → describe something → Create. The MiniApp tab opens on the template page (which, per FR-026, tells the user "the agent is writing it in the AI tab"). The bottom panel does not open, the AI tab contains no session for it, and the user has no way to watch, redirect or stop the agent that is writing their MiniApp.

defects.summary: All Previewers cannot expand a collapsed preview column: `previewCollapsed` is written but nothing reads it to drive the panel, so the FR-040 tutorial route opens the list inside a zero-width column.
defects.repro:
frontend/src/components/DataPreview.tsx:94 — `openAllPreviewers()` does `useAppStore.setState({ previewCollapsed: false })`, and its doc comment at :83-88 asserts "`ProjectWorkspace` owns the panel handle that turns that flag into an expanded column." It does not. Grep for `previewCollapsed` across frontend/src returns only: uiSlice.ts:17 (initial value), uiSlice.ts:110 (`togglePreview`), store/index.ts:95 (persist), store/types.ts:366 (type), and this write. ProjectWorkspace.tsx:521-533 has the analogous effect for the LEFT panel (`paletteCollapsed` → `paletteRef.collapse()/expand()`), but the preview `ResizablePanel` at ProjectWorkspace.tsx:776-786 takes only `panelRef={previewPanelRef}` and has no `collapsed` binding and no effect reading the flag.

User repro: drag the right preview column shut (it is `collapsible collapsedSize="0%"`), then run the `welcome-to-scistudio` tutorial to its `where-previewers-live` step. useLearningCenter.ts:317-323 calls `applyStepRoute` → targets.ts:363 `handlers.showAllPreviewers()` → `openAllPreviewers()`. The flag flips, the column stays at 0%, the PreviewerPalette mounts inside it invisibly, and the step rings nothing — the exact failure targets.ts:276-279 says the required (non-optional) handler exists to make impossible.

It compounds with FR-020: a MiniApp tab collapses the column programmatically (MiniAppTab.tsx:159-166), so the same step run while a MiniApp is focused is guaranteed to land on a collapsed column. The underlying dead flag is pre-existing — `Ctrl/Cmd+D` (useAppKeyboardShortcuts.ts:68 → `togglePreview`) has been a no-op for the same reason — but FR-033 states the expansion as a MUST and the new code depends on it.

defects.summary: The promotion confirm dialog calls a MiniApp a "data type": the new `miniapp` kind falls through a non-exhaustive noun chain.
defects.repro:
frontend/src/components/promotion/UserLibraryDialogs.tsx:75-80 — `const noun = plan.item.kind === "block" ? "block" : plan.item.kind === "previewer" ? "previewer" : "data type";`. frontend/src/components/promotion/promotable.ts:43 widened `PromotableItem["kind"]` to `"block" | "type" | "previewer" | "miniapp"` and added `promotableMiniApp()` (:224-232), and frontend/src/components/promotion/promoteToUserLibrary.ts:488-501 `promoteDirectory` routes a MiniApp through the same `prompts.confirm`. The chain is an if/else on a union, not a `switch` with an exhaustiveness check, so the new member typechecks its way into the last arm.

User repro: activity bar → MiniApps → hover a project-tier MiniApp card → Promote to My Library. The dialog reads "Move the data type Threshold Explorer into your personal library as threshold-explorer." The dependency warning at :124 repeats it ("Without them this data type will fail to load"), and the surrounding sentence at :91-93 says "Its file leaves this project" for what is a whole directory.

defects.summary: A stale per-panel change counter makes a freshly opened MiniApp tear down and respawn its process 500 ms after it opens.
defects.repro:
frontend/src/miniapps/MiniAppTab.tsx:44-52 — `changeSeq` is read from the session-long store counter `panelFilesChangedSeq[tab.panelId]`, and the effect fires on MOUNT for any non-zero value, not only on a value that moved while this pane was alive. The counter is bumped by uiSlice.ts:123-130 for every `panel.files_changed` frame and is never reset per tab.

User repro: open MiniApp X; let the agent (or your own editor) write into its directory, so `panelFilesChangedSeq["X"]` reaches 1+ and the tab reloads correctly; close the tab; open X again, on the same or a different output. 500 ms after the new tab appears, `reloadKey` goes 0 → 1, the just-created context is DELETEd (killing the panel.py that has only just finished starting) and a second one is created — a visible flash and a wasted process cycle on every subsequent open of that panel for the rest of the session. The fix is to latch the mount-time value and reload only on a change past it.

defects.summary: A focused MiniApp tab still shows the full workflow toolbar (Run/Pause/Stop/Reset/Delete/Add annotation), contradicting the stated reason `miniapp` was added to `activeTabKind`.
defects.repro:
frontend/src/App.parts/useActiveTab.ts:33-45 justifies adding `miniapp` to the union thus: "without it a MiniApp tab would put the workflow toolbar over a surface that has no canvas underneath it." But frontend/src/components/Toolbar.tsx:138 derives only `const isFileTab = activeTabKind === "file";` and :213 renders `{!isFileTab && <WorkflowGroups .../>}`. `miniapp` is not `file`, so `!isFileTab` is true and the whole workflow group renders.

User repro: open a MiniApp tab. Run, Pause, Stop, Reset, Delete block and Add annotation sit above a pane with no canvas; pressing Run starts the backing workflow with no visual feedback on screen. Behaviour matches the `preview` kind, so this is a comment that overstates what the change achieved rather than a regression — but the guard the comment describes does not exist.

area: ADR-054 Phase D MiniApp panel-process teardown vs. API responsiveness (SC-005 / FR-011 / FR-012 / US7): "while a panel.py hangs or crashes, the API answers a health request within one second"
how_you_tried: Read src/scistudio/panels/contexts.py, process.py, process_config.py, api/routes/panels.py, api/ws.py, engine/events.py to map every caller that can hold PanelContexts.lock or run a blocking stop on the event loop. Then ran a REAL uvicorn server (free port 49702, never 8000) on the worktree source against a temp project at /tmp/adv054-proj, using the same runtime stand-in the repo's own panel route tests use, with the real panels router, the real panels_lifespan, and the product's real GET /api/version mounted as a probe alongside an async /health and a sync /health-sync (the two shapes the product ships: /api/version is async, /api/runs/_health is sync). Shipped defaults throughout (SCISTUDIO_PANEL_TEARDOWN_GRACE=5); no limits weakened. Started MiniApps from four panel.py fixtures: hang-in-setup, hang-in-setup+SIGTERM-ignored, hang-in-teardown (plain), hang-in-teardown+SIGTERM-ignored. Timed health from separate client threads on fresh connections every 100 ms, plus an in-server event-loop lag probe. Scenarios: (S1) DELETE close of 4 wedged MiniApps; (S2) the tab's Stop button while a workflow event reaches the store on the API loop the way the scheduler emits it; (S3a) project switch then the next workflow event; (S3b) project switch then a panel HTTP request holding the lock while an event arrives on the loop; (S3c) project switch plus 45 concurrent panel requests with NO event-loop caller at all; (S4) SIGTERM shutdown with 6 wedged MiniApps open. S1 holds — DELETE close is 0.03 s, health max 0.016 s, loop lag 0.003 s; that is the one path the existing SC-005 test (tests/panels/test_miniapp_context.py:434) actually covers. Every other teardown path broke the one-second bound, reproducibly across repeated runs. Repro scripts: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jiazhenz-SciStudio/f2d97285-411f-4389-ad37-b816cc187546/scratchpad/adv/{server.py,drive.py,make_project.py,s3.py,s4.py,s5.py,s6.py,s7.py,s8.py}. Note: .workflow/records/2354-feat-2354-miniapp-phase-d.json shows as modified in the worktree, written by a concurrent pytest/hook run, not by me.

defects.summary: PanelContexts.stop_process() calls PanelProcess.stop() while holding the store RLock, so the tab's Stop button on a hung MiniApp freezes the whole API for the full teardown grace plus kill window — measured 4.7 s and 9.75 s health latency against a 1 s bound.
defects.repro:
Server: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jiazhenz-SciStudio/f2d97285-411f-4389-ad37-b816cc187546/scratchpad/adv/server.py /tmp/adv054-proj <free-port>, launched with HOME=/tmp/adv054-home and PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src. Driver: scratchpad/adv/s3.py (plain teardown hang) and s2b.py (teardown hang that ignores SIGTERM), probe s8.py for the product's own /api/version.
1. POST /api/panels/contexts {kind:miniapp, panel_id:lab.teardownsoft} and wait for state=running. panel.py is: def setup(data): pass / def teardown(): while True: time.sleep(3600).
2. POST /api/panels/contexts/<id>/process/stop from one client thread.
3. 0.3 s later, emit a workflow event on the API event loop the way the scheduler does (await event_bus.emit(EngineEvent('block_done', block_id='seg', data={'workflow_id':'wf'}))). PanelContexts.on_event takes self.lock and blocks.
Measured (two independent runs): POST /process/stop 5.053 s / 5.016 s; the loop-side emit 4.745 s / 4.712 s; GET /health (async) max 4.728 s / 4.692 s; GET /health-sync (threadpool) max 4.717 s / 4.692 s; the product's real GET /api/version max 4.707 s; server-side event-loop lag 4.739 s. With teardown additionally ignoring SIGTERM (lab.teardown): POST /process/stop 10.08 s, emit 9.76 s, /health 9.751 s, /health-sync 9.730 s, loop lag 9.744 s. Every one of these is a single health sample over 1 s, up to 9.75x the bound.
Cause: src/scistudio/panels/contexts.py:419-425 — 'with self.lock: ... context.process.stop()'. PanelProcess.stop (src/scistudio/panels/process.py) joins its worker for teardown_grace()+5 s, then terminates the tree with another grace and reaps, all inside the lock. close_all() was fixed to stop off the lock; stop_process() was not. Any loop-side lock user then blocks the event loop: on_event (contexts.py:172, awaited on the API loop by EventBus.emit) and close_for_client (contexts.py:469, called from the WS disconnect task at src/scistudio/api/ws.py:292).

defects.summary: close_all()'s _join_stopping is not off the lock as its docstring claims — _synchronize() calls it with the lock already held, and via on_event it runs the join directly on the API event loop; a project switch with MiniApps open froze the loop 5.0-5.3 s.
defects.repro:
Driver: scratchpad/adv/s4.py (loop path) and s5.py (lock-held path).
S3a (join runs ON the event loop): open 3 MiniApps on lab.teardownsoft (hang in teardown), wait for running; POST /x/switch to replace runtime.active_project (what opening another project does — project_identity uses id(project)); then emit block_done on the loop. on_event -> _synchronize (contexts.py:115-118) sees the identity changed -> close_all -> _join_stopping (contexts.py:139) waits teardown_grace()+5 s ON THE LOOP. Measured twice: emit 5.297 s / 5.032 s; GET /health max 5.299 s / 5.029 s; /health-sync max 5.302 s / 5.019 s; server loop lag 5.282 s / 5.010 s. Ceiling is 10 s at shipped defaults.
S3b (join held under the lock): open 4 MiniApps on lab.hang (setup hangs, SIGTERM ignored); POST /x/switch; then GET /api/panels/contexts/<id>/process from a client thread — that threadpool request enters get() -> 'with self.lock' -> _synchronize -> close_all, and _join_stopping runs inside the caller's still-held RLock; 0.3 s later emit block_done on the loop. Measured: panel GET 5.108 s (404 stale, as expected), loop-side emit 4.794 s, /health max 4.789 s, /health-sync max 4.801 s, loop lag 4.782 s.
Cause: close_all (contexts.py:124-139) places _join_stopping after its own 'with self.lock' block, but its only two callers are the async lifespan and _synchronize (contexts.py:118) — and every _synchronize caller (get, create, by_token, artifact, claim_writeback, on_event) is already inside 'with self.lock'. RLock reentrancy means the join still runs under the lock. The docstring's guarantee ('the lock a health request needs is never held while a hung panel.py is being killed (SC-005)') does not hold on the path that actually runs.

defects.summary: With no event-loop caller involved at all, panel requests queued on the store lock during a close_all join exhaust the anyio threadpool and starve sync routes — the shape GET /api/runs/_health has — measured 5.02 s.
defects.repro:
Driver: scratchpad/adv/s6.py. Open 4 MiniApps on lab.hang; POST /x/switch; then fire 45 concurrent GET /api/panels/contexts/<id>/process (the tab polls each open MiniApp's process status, and panel call/read are sync routes too). One request runs close_all's 5 s join under the lock; the other 44 block on the lock, each pinning an anyio worker thread (default limiter 40).
Measured: 45 panel GETs max 5.039 s; GET /health-sync max 5.022 s (one sample over 1 s); GET /health (async) max 0.070 s; server loop lag 0.007 s — i.e. the loop was fine and the sync health route still missed the bound purely from threadpool starvation. The product's health-ish endpoint GET /api/runs/_health (src/scistudio/api/routes/runs.py:50-51) is a sync def and has exactly this exposure.

defects.summary: panels_lifespan runs close_all() (and its up-to-10 s join) inline on the event loop at shutdown, adding seconds to quit with wedged MiniApps open — 5.22 s measured.
defects.repro:
Driver: scratchpad/adv/s7.py. Open 4 lab.hang plus 2 lab.teardownsoft contexts, then SIGTERM the server while polling /health every 100 ms. Measured: the process exited 5.219 s after SIGTERM (ceiling teardown_grace()+5 = 10 s), with the delay spent in store.close_all() at src/scistudio/api/routes/panels.py:923, awaited nowhere — it is a blocking join inside the async lifespan's finally.
Health during this window is refused rather than slow (uvicorn stops accepting before lifespan shutdown), so this is a quit-latency defect rather than a health-latency one — filed P2 for that reason. It still contradicts the structural half of the claim (close_all must not block the loop), and on the desktop it eats into the main process's backend-exit timeout.

defects.summary: The SC-005 regression test covers only store.close(), the single teardown path that does not block — stop_process, the _synchronize/close_all path, and the lifespan shutdown are untested.
defects.repro: tests/panels/test_miniapp_context.py:434 test_closing_a_hanging_panel_answers_at_once asserts closed < 1.0 and answered < 1.0 for store.close(hanging.context_id) only, and lowers SCISTUDIO_PANEL_TEARDOWN_GRACE to 0.5 while doing it. My S1 confirms that path is genuinely fast at shipped defaults (4 wedged MiniApps, DELETE close 0.028 s, health max 0.016 s, loop lag 0.003 s). Nothing exercises PanelContexts.stop_process, a project switch through _synchronize -> close_all, or panels_lifespan shutdown, which is why three over-budget paths survive. Suggested additions: assert that a store.get() from another thread returns under 1 s while stop_process is in flight, and that _synchronize-triggered close_all does not hold self.lock across the join.

area: ADR-054 MiniApp process lifecycle (SC-004 / FR-008 / FR-013): "ten seconds after a MiniApp tab closes — or after the grace period once its browser has disconnected — no process of its tree is alive, on Windows and POSIX, including a panel.py that starts a child process"
how_you_tried:
Read /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/src/scistudio/panels/process.py, contexts.py, process_config.py, bootstrap.py, /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/src/scistudio/api/ws.py, /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/src/scistudio/engine/runners/process_handle.py and platform.py, plus /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/src/scistudio/api/app.py (shutdown order), /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/src/scistudio/api/routes/panels.py, /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/frontend/src/panels/PanelFrame.tsx, frontend/src/miniapps/MiniAppTab.tsx and frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts (what actually closes a context on tab close and where ws_client_id comes from).

Then RAN real panel processes. Four throwaway pytest files under /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/ (test_break_sc004.py, test_break2.py, test_break3.py, test_break4.py), executed with `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src /opt/anaconda3/envs/scistudio/bin/python -m pytest <file> -q -s -p no:cacheprovider` from the worktree root. Each launches a real subprocess via start_panel_process with a hostile panel.py, then closes the context and samples liveness with psutil off a background thread (so the measurement is not serialised behind the blocking stop()).

Attacks executed: (a) panel.py spawns a child and the root leaves with os._exit during setup; (b) same, root leaves mid-serve from inside a call; (c) child spawned with start_new_session=True; (d) panel.py installs SIG_IGN for SIGTERM and hangs forever in teardown; (e) context closed while a call is in flight (panel sleeping 300s, SIGTERM ignored); (f) PanelContexts.close_all — the project-switch/lifespan path — with an in-flight call; (g) the full backend-shutdown sequence from app.py (close_all() then registry.terminate_all(5.0)); (h) close_for_client against a context whose ws_client_id is None; (i) a PanelProcessHandle whose started_at is 3s later than the root's create_time (what happens when Popen takes longer than the 2s tolerance to return); (j) a simulated Windows handle whose Job Object assignment failed (pgid=None, job_active_process_count()->0, terminate_job_object()->True).

Baseline sanity check: a well-behaved panel.py with a child dies in 0.03s, so the harness is not just measuring its own overhead.

Platform caveat: everything was measured on macOS (POSIX). The Windows half of the claim is UNVERIFIED — I have no Windows host. The Windows defect below is a code-path simulation plus a direct comparison with the repo's own ADR-055 run_command containment, not a live Windows repro.

I did not modify the repository; all files written are under /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/. (Note: `git status` in the worktree shows .workflow/records/2354-feat-2354-miniapp-phase-d.json modified — that is from a concurrent full-suite xdist run at 00:29-00:36 local, not from my runs, which touched nothing under .workflow/.) All processes I spawned were reaped; a final `ps` shows no survivors.

defects.summary: When the panel root process exits on its own (crash, os._exit, segfault), PanelProcess._on_exit deregisters the registry handle WITHOUT terminating the process group, and the later stop() skips termination because popen.poll() is no longer None — so any child panel.py started is orphaned permanently and is unreachable by both close and backend shutdown.
defects.repro: pytest /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/test_break_sc004.py -k A1 (and -k A2). panel.py: `p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-c','import time; time.sleep(900)']); os._exit(0)` at import time (A1) or from inside a call (A2). Measured, 4/4 runs of A2 and 1/1 of A1: `state=crashed child_pid=<pid> alive_after_stop=True registry_after_crash=[] alive_after_terminate_all=True`. The registry is EMPTY right after the crash, so ProcessRegistry.terminate_all at shutdown has nothing to terminate. The child survives the tab close, the backend shutdown, and outlives the app. Note _serve_calls' id-mismatch branch DOES call _terminate_tree before _on_exit; the OSError/ProtocolError branch (the common crash path) does not.

defects.summary: A child that leaves the panel's process group survives every termination path, including full backend shutdown. _posix_group_members matches members only by getpgid(pid)==pgid, so subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True) — exactly what the repo's own PosixOps.create_process_group sets for every engine subprocess — escapes the kill.
defects.repro: pytest /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/test_break_sc004.py -k A3 → `stop() took 0.05s; child_pid=21847 alive_after_stop=True alive_after_terminate_all=True`. And the full shutdown sequence, pytest /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/test_break3.py -k C2 → `close_all returned at 10.02s, terminate_all returned at 15.11s; root alive=False detached child (pid 42187) alive=True`. A panel.py that launches work through the engine's own spawn helpers (which set start_new_session=True) hits this without doing anything unusual; a double-fork daemon does too.

defects.summary: Windows: assign_to_job's return value is discarded at launch, and live_members() then believes the (empty) Job Object over the demonstrably live root — owns_live_process() returns False, so shutdown's terminate_all drops the handle without terminating, and _stop() reports success after TerminateJobObject on an empty job.
defects.repro: pytest /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/test_break2.py -k B2 — builds a PanelProcessHandle over a real live panel root with pgid=None (what __init__ does on win32) and a platform-ops stub whose job_active_process_count returns 0 and terminate_job_object returns True: `owns_live_process=False live_members=0 alive after terminate_all=True registry=[]`. There is also a launch race: the panel is NOT created suspended, so it can fork children between Popen returning and AssignProcessToJobObject. Compare the repo's own ADR-055 containment in src/scistudio/ai/agent/mcp/tools_execution.py:553-585 and :776-778, which creates the process with CREATE_SUSPENDED, requires `assign_to_job(...) and resume_process(...)` to both succeed, and refuses to run the command otherwise (_JOB_OBJECT_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE). NOT verified on a real Windows host.

defects.summary: Closing a tab while a call is in flight takes about 15 seconds, not 10: stop() joins the pipe worker for teardown_grace+5 = 10s (the worker cannot read the shutdown sentinel until the in-flight call returns), and only then starts the 5s SIGTERM grace.
defects.repro: pytest /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/test_break2.py -k B1. panel.py ignores SIGTERM, spawns a child, and has `def slow(): time.sleep(300)`; a thread issues the call, then stop() is invoked 1s later. Tree liveness (root, child) sampled from a separate thread: `{5.0: (True, True), 10.0: (True, True), 11.0: (True, True), 16.0: (False, False), 20.0: (False, False)}`. Same shape via the project-switch path, test_break2.py -k B3: `close_all returned after 10.03s, tree at return=(True, True), at t=10s=(True, True), at t=17s=(False, False)`.

defects.summary: Even the simplest hostile panel exceeds the ten seconds: the design budget is 5s waiting out teardown plus a 5s SIGTERM grace = exactly 10.0s, with zero slack for overhead, so the root is still alive at t=10.0s.
defects.repro: pytest /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/test_break4.py -k D2. panel.py: `signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)` plus `def teardown(): while True: time.sleep(0.5)`. Root alive sampled at fixed marks: `{9.5: True, 10.0: True, 10.5: False, 11.0: False}`. test_break_sc004.py -k A4 measured the same case at 10.31s. Baseline for contrast (test_break4.py -k D1, cooperative panel with a child): stop() returns at 0.03s with root and child both dead.

defects.summary: A MiniApp opened while the websocket is reconnecting is created with ws_client_id = None and is therefore exempt from the FR-013 disconnect sweep forever — if that browser then dies without sending the DELETE, its panel.py process runs until the backend exits.
defects.file: /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/src/scistudio/panels/contexts.py:466-476 (close_for_client matches only `context.ws_client_id == ws_client_id`) and :383 (`ws_client_id=payload.get("ws_client_id")`, unvalidated); /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/frontend/src/miniapps/MiniAppTab.tsx:95 (`...(wsClientId ? { ws_client_id: wsClientId } : {})`); frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.parts/handleMiniApp.ts:83-84 + frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:141 (handleWsDisconnected sets wsClientId to null on every close)

Related: ws.py:253-271 (_client_id_for) documents that a reconnecting client quotes the id it was given so its MiniApp survives a flaky connection — the shipped frontend never does this (useWebSocket.ts:75 `const url = wsUrl("/ws")`, no client_id query), so that branch is dead code and every reconnect mints a fresh id.

defects.summary: Latent race: the ±2s create-time filter in _posix_group_members makes a handle disown its own live tree when Popen takes longer than 2s to return, because started_at is sampled after Popen — live_members() returns 0, terminate_all drops the handle, and _stop_group reports 'process group already empty' while root and child keep running.
defects.file: /Users/jiazhenz/SciStudio/.worktrees/adr054-phase-d/src/scistudio/panels/process.py:79 (`if (proc.info.get("create_time") or 0.0) + _START_TIME_TOLERANCE_SECONDS < started_at: continue`) and :580 (`started_at=time.time()` sampled after subprocess.Popen and assign_to_job)
defects.repro: pytest /tmp/miniapp-adversarial/test_break4.py -k D3 — constructs PanelProcessHandle(pid=<live panel root>, started_at=time.time()+3.0, job_object=None), i.e. the state produced by a Popen that took 3s to return: `live_members=0 owns_live_process=False _stop detail='process group already empty'; root alive=True child alive=True`. Fork+exec of a large-RSS backend on a loaded machine can plausibly exceed 2s; nothing in the code bounds it.

area: ADR-054 Phase D — panel context capability confinement (SC-003 / FR-003 / FR-017): no process on preview/interactive contexts, `call` unavailable, and `panel.py` source unreachable through the token-scoped asset route.
how_you_tried:
Read contexts.py, descriptor.py, process.py, files.py, sdk/1/scistudio-panel.js, frontend/src/panels/bridge.ts, plus api/routes/panels.py and PanelFrame.tsx (the two seams the brief did not name but that actually enforce the claim).

Then ran three live probes (all artifacts under /tmp/adr054-probe; the repository was not modified by me).

BACKEND (FastAPI TestClient over the real router, panel `lab.explorer` declaring contexts ["preview","miniapp"] with a real panel.py carrying a unique source marker) — 74 checks in /tmp/adr054-probe/probe.py:
- Preview mount: operations == ["read"], services == ["open","save"], process == null, context.process is None, context.watcher is None, ProcessRegistry.active_handles() == [], and psutil showed zero new child processes after a 1s settle.
- Interactive mount on a panel declaring ["interactive","miniapp"] (real `interactive_prompt` event through the EventBus, paused block state, live `_interactive_futures`): operations == ["writeBack"], process null, no subprocess, registry empty.
- Raw `POST /contexts/{id}/call` on both preview and interactive → 400 `unsupported` ("This context does not provide call"), including fn="setup", "teardown", "__import__", "SECRET_TOKEN".
- `POST .../process/restart` on preview and interactive → 400 and, verified with psutil, started nothing. `GET .../process` → 404.
- kind spoofing ("Miniapp", "MINIAPP", "miniapp ", "mini app", "previewminiapp", ["miniapp"], null) → all 400/422, nothing spawned.
- A preview-only panel asked for a miniapp context → 409 context_mismatch, nothing spawned; parse_descriptor emits the "Python is never started" note.
- 34 asset-route spellings of panel.py: case (panel.PY/Panel.Py/PANEL.PY), url-encoding (%2E, %2e, %70anel), double-encoding (..%252F), traversal (sub/../, ..%2F, %2e%2e/, //, /, backslash), trailing dot/space/%20/%00, NTFS stream suffix, `panel.py/`, `panel.py/.`, `panel.py?.js`, `panel.py#.js`, plus fully quote()'d variants — every one refused 404 with an FR-026 code. A genuine `.js` copy of the same bytes IS served, proving the leak detector works.
- Symlinks: `alias.js -> panel.py`, `alias.json -> panel.py`, `sub/up.js -> ../panel.py`, `outside.json -> /etc/hosts` — all refused (realpath + commonpath + suffix). lib/ and sdk/ escape attempts refused.
- HARDLINK: `hard.js` hardlinked to panel.py → **200 with the module source verbatim**. Escalated in probe3.py: hardlinking panel.py to `index.html` makes parse_descriptor accept it as a valid `entry` (no diagnostic note), and the token entry route serves panel.py's source with the bootstrap script prepended.

FRONTEND (real bridge.ts under vitest/jsdom over a MessageChannel, /tmp/adr054-probe/fe, 6/6 pass): a page posting a raw `{type:"call"}` on its port after ready() is refused `unsupported` on a preview context and on an interactive context, the handler is never invoked, case/prototype variants ("Call","CALL"," call","__proto__","constructor","toString") are all refused, an empty operations array refuses even `read`, `call` is forwarded only when the backend granted it, and a call before ready() is `not_ready`. Also confirmed the init payload hands the page `basePath`/`sdkUrl`/`libBaseUrl` (which carry the token) but never `context_id`, and the iframe is `sandbox="allow-scripts"` with `connect-src 'none'`, so a preview page has no address for the call route even if it wanted one.

NO-EXECUTION PROOF: rewrote panel.py to write a sentinel file at import time, re-scanned the descriptor and exercised every preview operation (create, read, renew, open, process/stop, process/restart, call, asset fetch). The sentinel was never created — discovery and preview never import panel.py.

TEST-SUITE CLAIM ("100% of preview and interactive context tests"): instrumented subprocess.Popen inside scistudio.panels.process with a pytest plugin and ran tests/panels + the six panel API suites serially. 40 panel subprocess launches, every one attributable to tests/panels/test_miniapp_context.py, tests/panels/test_panel_process.py, or tests/api/test_panel_call_route.py's miniapp tests; zero from any preview or interactive test. 187 tests pass, exit 0.

So the literal SC-003 sentence survived everything I threw at it. What did not survive is the FR-017 half the brief asked me to attack: the asset route's confinement is defeated by a hardlink, because os.path.realpath cannot see one.

Unrelated observation: while I worked, .workflow/records/2354-*.json and five tests/integration + tests/contract files were being rewritten by a concurrent xdist run in this same worktree (popen-gw* temp paths in the ledger findings, timestamps inside my session window). None of those are files I selected or touched — something else is running tests in this worktree.

defects.summary: resolve_panel_file's suffix guard is defeated by a hardlink: os.path.realpath resolves symlinks but not hardlinks, so any hardlink of panel.py carrying an allowed suffix is served verbatim through the token asset route — including as the panel's `entry`, which parse_descriptor accepts without a diagnostic while it rejects a symlinked entry.
defects.repro:
Repro A (any allowed suffix), /tmp/adr054-probe/probe.py:
  panel dir lab.explorer declares contexts ["preview","miniapp"], panel.py contains SECRET_TOKEN='panel-py-source-marker-9f3a'
  os.link(panel_dir/'panel.py', panel_dir/'hard.js')
  open a PREVIEW context, then GET /api/panels/t/{token}/assets/lab.explorer/hard.js
  observed: 200, body == panel.py source. (GET .../panel.py is 404 'FR-026: file type is not a panel asset', and a symlink alias.js -> panel.py is 404 as well, so only the hardlink slips through.)

Repro B (escalation to the entry document), /tmp/adr054-probe/probe3.py:
  os.link(panel_dir/'panel.py', panel_dir/'index.html')   # entry defaults to index.html
  parse_descriptor(...) -> succeeds, entry='index.html', has_python=True, notes == []   (a SYMLINKED index.html -> panel.py is rejected: realpath hits the .py suffix)
  open a preview context, GET /api/panels/t/{token}/assets/lab.explorer/index.html
  observed: 200 text/html, bootstrap script + the full panel.py source (API_KEY='entry-hardlink-marker-7c21'), i.e. the module source is delivered into the iframe document.

Precondition: write access to the panel directory (the panel author, or the agent that scaffolds a MiniApp under permission_mode=bypass). Not reachable by a remote or by the panel page itself, which is why this is P3 and not higher. The gap is that files.py:58 documents the guard as rejecting 'symlink escapes and executable source' and the check is link-type-blind: a stat-based inode/nlink check, or refusing any path whose inode matches panel.py, would close it. The descriptor's asymmetry (symlinked entry rejected, hardlinked entry silently accepted with no note) is the same root cause.

defects.summary: POST /contexts/{id}/process/stop has no kind or process guard, so it answers 200 for a preview or interactive context, unlike restart (400 unsupported) and GET process (404 no_process).
defects.repro: Open a preview context on lab.explorer, then POST /api/panels/contexts/{id}/process/stop -> 200 with a full ContextResponse whose "process" is null (observed in /tmp/adr054-probe/probe.py). PanelContexts.stop_process (contexts.py:419) only checks `if context.process is not None`, so a kind that can never own a process is accepted rather than refused. Nothing is started or stopped, so this is a contract inconsistency rather than a capability leak: the three process endpoints disagree about what a non-miniapp context should get back, and a client that treats a 200 from stop as proof the context had a process will be wrong.

defects.summary: PanelContext.provides() grants the miniapp kind ["read","call"] without consulting panel.has_python, so a MiniApp with no panel.py advertises an operation whose every invocation is refused 400.
defects.repro:
Register a panel declaring contexts ["preview","miniapp"] with panel.py deleted (has_python=False), then POST /api/panels/contexts {kind:'miniapp', panel_id:'lab.explorer', source:{...}}.
  observed: 200 with operations == ["read","call"] and process == null (_create_miniapp only starts a process `if panel.has_python`, contexts.py:341).
  POST /contexts/{id}/call {fn:'echo'} -> 400 unsupported ("This context does not provide call"), because the route also requires context.process is not None.
The SDK therefore defines api.call for that page (scistudio-panel.js gates on operations.indexOf("call")), and the bridge forwards it, and the backend then denies it — the page is told it has a capability the host will always refuse. Does not break SC-003 (preview and interactive are still correct), but provides() should mirror the route's own precondition, e.g. return ["read"] when not panel.has_python. Reproduced in /tmp/adr054-probe/probe.py, section 7.
